title: Base change along a purely inseparable extension is a homeomorphism
statement:
Let $k\subset k'$ be a purely inseparable field extension and $X$ a
scheme over $k$. Then the canonical morphism $X_{k'}\to X$ is a
homeomorphism of underlying topological spaces.

proof.text: Let $\pi:\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the morphism induced by the inclusion $k\to k'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Since $k'/k$ is purely inseparable, $\pi$ is integral, universally injective and surjective [lem-pc-spec-pure-insep-integral-radicial-surjective].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01S4 (morphisms-lemma-universally-injective); Algebra, Section 0BR5 (algebra-section-universal-homeomorphism), opening paragraph

proof.text: By [lem-pc-integral-radicial-surjective-universal-homeomorphism], an integral, universally injective and surjective morphism is a universal homeomorphism; hence $\pi$ is a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]: for every morphism of schemes $Y'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ the projection $Y'\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'\to Y'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is a homeomorphism.

Let $s:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism of the $k$-scheme $X$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. By [def-pc-base-change] (with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}k'$), $X_{k'}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] and the canonical morphism $X_{k'}\to X$ is its projection to $X$. This is the projection of step 2 for $Y'=X$, $Y'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ the morphism $s$ (the fibre product being symmetric in its two factors), hence a homeomorphism of underlying topological spaces.

source.place: Morphisms, Definition 04DD (morphisms-definition-universal-homeomorphism), instance of the definition
